records.source: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־יֵה֣וּא בֶן־חֲנָ֔נִי עַל־בַּעְשָׁ֖א לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jehu son of Hanani, a word against Baasha:

L.1: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

R.1: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave a message to Jehu son of Hanani, a message against Baasha. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said,

decisions.choice: Jehu son of Hanani: a prophet in the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: This Jehu is not the later King Jehu (2 Kings 9). He is called "the prophet" in verses 7 and 12. A seer named Hanani spoke against Asa king of Judah (2 Chronicles 16:7), and Jehu son of Hanani later rebuked Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 19:2; 20:34).

decisions.choice: against Baasha: the prophet who condemned Jeroboam's house is followed by one who condemns Baasha's
decisions.reason: Baasha had seized the throne by killing Nadab and wiping out the house of Jeroboam, as Ahijah had foretold (15:27-30; 14:10-11). Now the same kind of word is spoken against Baasha himself.

decisions.choice: gave a message ... The LORD said
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the LORD gave the prophet a message, and names the speaker of the words that follow.

records.source: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֲרִימֹתִ֨יךָ֙ מִן־הֶ֣עָפָ֔ר וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֣ נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ׀בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֗ם וַֽתַּחֲטִא֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִיסֵ֖נִי בְּחַטֹּאתָֽם׃
records.gloss: Because that I raised you from the dust and made you ruler over my people Israel, and you have walked in [the] way of Jeroboam and made sin my people Israel, to provoke me with their sins,
pieces: "I lifted you up from the dust and made you ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. Yet you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and led {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to sin, provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with their sins.

L.2: "Because I lifted you up from the dust and made you ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam and have made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel sin, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with their sins,

R.2: "I lifted you up from nothing and made you the leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. But you have lived the way Jeroboam lived, and you have led {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel into sin. They have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with their sins.

decisions.choice: raised you from the dust: lifted you from a low and unknown place
decisions.reason: Dust stands for the lowest place (1 Samuel 2:8). Baasha came from an unimportant family of the tribe of Issachar (15:27), and Yahweh says he owes his throne to him.

decisions.choice: ruler: the one appointed by Yahweh to lead his people
decisions.reason: The word *nagid* names a leader whom Yahweh has chosen and set over his people, as with Saul, David and Jeroboam (1 Samuel 9:16; 2 Samuel 7:8; 14:7). Baasha's throne was his to hold under Yahweh.

decisions.choice: walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin: the standing charge against the kings of Israel
decisions.reason: Jeroboam made the golden calves at Bethel and Dan and led Israel to worship there (12:28-33). From now on, Kings judges each king of Israel by whether he kept to this sin and led the people into it (verses 13, 19, 26). The verb "made sin" is causative: the king led the nation to sin.

decisions.choice: to provoke me to anger: so that Yahweh is roused to anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to vex or rouse to anger. It is the second half of the standing charge: the people's sin angers Yahweh (14:9, 15; verses 7, 13, 26, 33).

decisions.choice: made ... sin (Literal); led ... to sin (Balanced); led ... into sin (Readable); provoke to anger (Literal, Balanced); made angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: These two formulas recur through the chapter and through Kings; each level keeps one wording for them, as at 14:9 and 14:16 (verses 13, 19, 26, 33).

decisions.choice: from nothing
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the dust as a lowly beginning.

records.source: הִנְנִ֥י מַבְעִ֛יר אַחֲרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֖א וְאַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית֑וֹ וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣יתְךָ֔ כְּבֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֥ם בֶּן־נְבָֽט׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] sweeping away after Baasha and after his house, and I will make your house like [the] house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
pieces: So I am about to sweep away Baasha and his house after him, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

L.3: look, I [am] about to sweep away after Baasha and after his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

R.3: So I am going to wipe out Baasha and his family. I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

decisions.choice: sweep away after: clear away to the last trace
decisions.reason: The verb means to burn up or to clear out completely. With "after" it pictures clearing away everything that is left, as Ahijah said of Jeroboam's house: "as one burns up dung until it is all gone" (14:10).

decisions.choice: house: family and royal line
decisions.reason: "House" here means Baasha's family and descendants, the line that might have ruled after him, as with "the house of Jeroboam".

decisions.choice: after Baasha ... your house: Yahweh speaks of Baasha and then to him
decisions.reason: The sentence moves from speaking about Baasha to speaking to him directly, a change of person that is common in Hebrew speech.

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for "house" in the sense of a royal line.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable divide the long sentence of verses 2-3 and join the judgment to its reasons with "So".

records.source: הַמֵּ֤ת לְבַעְשָׁא֙ בָּעִ֔יר יֹֽאכְל֖וּ הַכְּלָבִ֑ים וְהַמֵּ֥ת לוֹ֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: The one who dies of Baasha in the city, will eat the dogs; and the one who dies of him in the field, will eat [the] birds of the heavens."
pieces: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."

L.4: The one belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and the one belonging to him who dies in the field, the birds of the heavens will eat."

R.4: Dogs will eat anyone in Baasha's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat anyone who dies out in the country."

decisions.choice: eaten by dogs and birds: left unburied, the worst disgrace
decisions.reason: To lie unburied was a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26). The words are the same as those spoken against the house of Jeroboam (14:11), and later against Ahab's house (21:24).

decisions.choice: the field: open country outside the towns
decisions.reason: The field is land away from the city, so the two halves of the verse cover every place where Baasha's family might die.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י בַעְשָׁ֛א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Baasha and what he did and his might, [are] they not written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did and his might, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.5: And the rest of the matters of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.5: Everything else Baasha did, and his great deeds, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: a royal record now lost
decisions.reason: The court record of the kings of Israel, as at 14:19. It has not survived.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question that means "they are written"
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. It is the standard closing formula for a reign in Kings.

decisions.choice: his might: his strength and deeds of power, especially in war
decisions.reason: The word is used of a king's military strength and achievements. Baasha fought Asa of Judah throughout his reign (15:16-22).

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel (Literal); the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel (Balanced); the history of the kings of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The source formula has one wording at each level throughout Kings (14:19, 29). Balanced and Readable turn the question into a statement (m2).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב בַּעְשָׁא֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵלָ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And lay down Baasha with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and reigned Elah his son in his place.
pieces: Baasha rested with his ancestors and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king in his place.

L.6: And Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.

R.6: Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: This is the formula Kings uses for a king's death (2:10; 14:20, 31). Baasha dies in peace; the judgment spoken against his house falls on his son (verses 11-13).

decisions.choice: Tirzah: the royal city of Israel at this time
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had lived there (14:17), and Baasha reigned from it (15:21, 33). It lay northeast of Shechem. Omri later moved the capital to Samaria (verses 23-24).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings (2:10).

records.source: וְגַ֡ם בְּיַד־יֵה֨וּא בֶן־חֲנָ֜נִי הַנָּבִ֗יא דְּבַר־יְהוָ֡ה הָיָה֩ אֶל־בַּעְשָׁ֨א וְאֶל־בֵּית֜וֹ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הָרָעָ֣ה׀אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה׀בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה לְהַכְעִיסוֹ֙ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֔יו לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבֵ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְעַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־הִכָּ֖ה אֹתֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And also by [the] hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet [the] word of Yahweh came against Baasha and against his house, and because of all the evil which he did in [the] eyes of Yahweh, to provoke him with [the] work of his hands, to be like [the] house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it.
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had also come through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his house. It came because of all the evil Baasha did in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger by the work of his hands, so that he became like the house of Jeroboam. It came also because he had struck that house down.

L.7: And also by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came against Baasha and against his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger with the work of his hands, being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.

R.7: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his family. This was because Baasha had done what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry by the work of his hands, and he became just like Jeroboam's family. It was also because Baasha had killed Jeroboam's family.

decisions.choice: and also: a summary that adds the reasons for the judgment
decisions.reason: The verse sums up verses 1-4 and adds a second reason the prophet's word gave, which verse 2 did not state.

decisions.choice: the work of his hands: his idols, or all his deeds
decisions.reason: The phrase can name idols made by human hands (Deuteronomy 4:28; 31:29), which fits the charge of following Jeroboam's calves. It can also mean what a person does in general. Both readings are possible here.

decisions.choice: because he struck it down: Baasha is guilty for destroying Jeroboam's house
decisions.reason: Baasha killed Nadab and the whole house of Jeroboam (15:27-29). Yahweh had foretold that end (14:10-11), but Baasha acted out of his own ambition, and then did the same sins. A later prophet speaks the same way of Jehu's bloodshed at Jezreel (Hosea 1:4). "It" may also be read "him", meaning Nadab; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: The prophet is the one through whom the word came.

decisions.choice: that house (Balanced); Jeroboam's family (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what "it" refers to, the house of Jeroboam (m3).

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ אֵלָ֨ה בֶן־בַּעְשָׁ֧א עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּתִרְצָ֖ה שְׁנָתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: In year twenty and six year of Asa king of Judah reigned Elah son of Baasha over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
pieces: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned two years.

L.8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel in Tirzah, two years.

R.8: Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in the twenty-sixth year that Asa was king of Judah. Elah ruled in Tirzah for two years.

decisions.choice: two years: counted as parts of years
decisions.reason: Elah began in Asa's twenty-sixth year and died in his twenty-seventh (verse 10). Kings counts any part of a year as a year of a reign, so his "two years" may have been little more than one.

decisions.choice: reigned (Literal); became king ... and he reigned (Balanced); became king ... ruled (Readable)
decisions.reason: The accession formula has one wording at each level throughout Kings. Literal follows the Hebrew; Readable splits it into two sentences.

records.heading: Elah and Zimri kings of Israel

records.source: וַיִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ עַבְדּ֣וֹ זִמְרִ֔י שַׂ֖ר מַחֲצִ֣ית הָרָ֑כֶב וְה֤וּא בְתִרְצָה֙ שֹׁתֶ֣ה שִׁכּ֔וֹר בֵּ֣ית אַרְצָ֔א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הַבַּ֖יִת בְּתִרְצָֽה׃
records.gloss: And conspired against him his servant Zimri, commander of half of the chariotry; and he [was] in Tirzah drinking drunk [in the] house of Arza who [was] over the house in Tirzah.
pieces: His official Zimri, commander of half the chariots, plotted against him. Elah was in Tirzah at the time, getting drunk in the house of Arza, the steward of the palace in Tirzah.

L.9: And his servant Zimri, commander of half of the chariots, conspired against him. And he [was] in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who [was] over the house in Tirzah.

R.9: Zimri, one of Elah's officials, made plans to kill him. Zimri was the commander of half of Elah's chariots. One day Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the house of Arza, the man in charge of the palace there.

decisions.choice: his servant: a royal officer
decisions.reason: Zimri was one of the king's own officers, a high one, commanding half of the chariot force. The word marks his duty to the king he betrayed.

decisions.choice: over the house: the steward who ran the royal household
decisions.reason: "Over the house" is a title for the official in charge of the palace and its affairs (4:6; 18:3; Isaiah 22:15). The king was drinking in his steward's own house.

decisions.choice: drinking drunk: drinking until he was drunk
decisions.reason: The two words together stress that Elah was helpless with drink while his army was at war (verse 15).

decisions.choice: his official (Balanced); one of Elah's officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As with "the king's servants" in Samuel and Kings, Literal keeps "servant" and Balanced and Readable say "official" for a king's officer.

decisions.choice: made plans to kill him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "conspired" by what the plot was for (verse 10).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א זִמְרִי֙ וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ וַיְמִיתֵ֔הוּ בִּשְׁנַת֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וָשֶׁ֔בַע לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And came Zimri and struck him and killed him in year twenty and seven of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
pieces: Zimri came in and struck him down, killing him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and he became king in his place.

L.10: And Zimri came in and struck him and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned in his place.

R.10: Zimri came in, attacked Elah and killed him. This was in the twenty-seventh year that Asa was king of Judah. Then Zimri became king in Elah's place.

decisions.choice: struck him and killed him: attacked him and put him to death
decisions.reason: The first verb is the blow, the second its result. The same pair is used of Baasha's killing of Nadab (15:27-28).

decisions.choice: reigned in his place: the third change of dynasty by violence
decisions.reason: Baasha had taken the throne from Jeroboam's son by murder (15:28); now Zimri takes it from Baasha's son the same way.

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י בְמָלְכ֜וֹ כְּשִׁבְתּ֣וֹ עַל־כִּסְא֗וֹ הִכָּה֙ אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֔א לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֥יר ל֖וֹ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֑יר וְגֹאֲלָ֖יו וְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when he reigned, when he sat on his throne, he struck all [the] house of Baasha; not he left to him one urinating against a wall, and his redeemers, and his friend.
pieces: As soon as he became king and sat on his throne, he struck down the whole house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, neither his family redeemers nor his friends.

L.11: And it happened, when he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down all the house of Baasha; he did not leave him one who urinates against a wall, neither his redeemers nor his friend.

R.11: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed Baasha's whole family. He did not leave a single man or boy alive, not even the relatives who could avenge them, or their friends.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: any male at all
decisions.reason: A coarse expression for every male, used in curses on a royal house (14:10; 21:21; 2 Kings 9:8) and by David in anger (1 Samuel 25:22, 34). It means none would be left to carry on the family line.

decisions.choice: his redeemers: the near relatives bound to defend and avenge the family
decisions.reason: The *go'el* was the close relative who bought back family land and avenged a killed kinsman (Leviticus 25:25; Numbers 35:19). Zimri left no one who might avenge Baasha's house or claim its throne.

decisions.choice: his friend: his supporters and close companions
decisions.reason: The singular "friend" stands for the whole group of the king's friends. "Friend" can also be a court title (4:5), so it may mean his trusted advisers.

decisions.choice: a single male (Balanced); a single man or boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the coarse expression (m1). Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: the relatives who could avenge them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the duty of the redeemer that matters here (m2).

records.source: וַיַּשְׁמֵ֣ד זִמְרִ֔י אֵ֖ת כָּל־בֵּ֣ית בַּעְשָׁ֑א כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל־בַּעְשָׁ֔א בְּיַ֖ד יֵה֥וּא הַנָּבִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And destroyed Zimri all [the] house of Baasha, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke against Baasha by [the] hand of Jehu the prophet,
pieces: So Zimri destroyed the whole house of Baasha, as the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said against Baasha through Jehu the prophet,

L.12: And Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet,

R.12: So Zimri wiped out Baasha's whole family, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had warned Baasha through the prophet Jehu.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh: the prophecy of verses 1-4 is fulfilled
decisions.reason: Kings often notes that a prophet's word came true (15:29; 2 Kings 10:17). Zimri's crime is the means by which Yahweh's word is carried out, yet it is still his own crime (compare verse 7).

decisions.choice: destroyed: wiped out completely
decisions.reason: The verb means to exterminate, to destroy so that nothing remains.

records.source: אֶ֚ל כָּל־חַטֹּ֣אות בַּעְשָׁ֔א וְחַטֹּ֖אות אֵלָ֣ה בְנ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֗וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶחֱטִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהַכְעִ֗יס אֶת־יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּהַבְלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: because of all [the] sins of Baasha and [the] sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and which they made sin Israel, to provoke Yahweh God of Israel with their vanities.
pieces: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of his son Elah, the sins they committed and by which they led Israel to sin, provoking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.

L.13: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and which they made Israel sin, to provoke {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel to anger with their worthless idols.

R.13: This happened because of all the sins of Baasha and his son Elah. They sinned, and they led Israel into sin. They made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, angry with their useless idols.

decisions.choice: their vanities: their worthless idols
decisions.reason: The word *hevel* means a breath or vapor, something empty and passing. Used of gods it calls idols nothing, powerless and useless (Deuteronomy 32:21; Jeremiah 8:19; 10:15). Here it names the gods and images Israel worshiped, including Jeroboam's calves.

decisions.choice: because of all the sins: the judgment falls for what Baasha and Elah did
decisions.reason: The writer gives the reason for the end of Baasha's house: the sins of the two kings and the sin they led Israel into (verse 2).

decisions.choice: worthless idols (Literal, Balanced); useless idols (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Deuteronomy 32:21, kept at each level wherever Kings uses this word for idols (verse 26).

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin; provoke to anger / made angry
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֵלָ֖ה וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Elah and all that he did, [are] they not written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.14: And the rest of the matters of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.14: Everything else Elah did is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record named in verse 5
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. The death and burial formula is missing for Elah, who was murdered (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the source formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַת֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֥ךְ זִמְרִ֛י שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּתִרְצָ֑ה וְהָעָ֣ם חֹנִ֔ים עַֽל־גִּבְּת֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: In year twenty and seven year of Asa king of Judah reigned Zimri seven days in Tirzah; and the people [were] encamping against Gibbethon, which [belonged] to the Philistines.
pieces: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri became king in Tirzah, and he reigned seven days. The troops were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.

L.15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. And the people [were] encamped against Gibbethon, which [belonged] to the Philistines.

R.15: Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year that Asa was king of Judah. He ruled in Tirzah for only seven days. At that time the army was camped near Gibbethon, a town that belonged to the Philistines, ready to attack it.

decisions.choice: the people: the army in the field
decisions.reason: Here "the people" means Israel's fighting men, camped against an enemy town (verse 16).

decisions.choice: Gibbethon: a town on the border with the Philistines
decisions.reason: Gibbethon had been given to Dan (Joshua 19:44) but was held by the Philistines. Nadab was besieging it when Baasha killed him (15:27), and Israel's army was there again at Zimri's coup, perhaps a generation later.

decisions.choice: seven days: the shortest reign of any king of Israel
decisions.reason: Zimri's reign ended within the week, as verses 16-18 tell.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: Where "the people" means the army in the field, Literal keeps "the people" and Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

decisions.choice: ready to attack it
decisions.reason: Readable explains that "encamped against" a town means besieging it.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָעָם֙ הַחֹנִ֣ים לֵאמֹ֔ר קָשַׁ֣ר זִמְרִ֔י וְגַ֖ם הִכָּ֣ה אֶת־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ כָֽל־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל אֶת־עָמְרִ֨י שַׂר־צָבָ֧א עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And heard the people encamping, saying, has conspired Zimri and also has struck the king; and made king all Israel Omri, commander of [the] army, over Israel on the day the that in the camp.
pieces: When the troops in the camp heard it said, "Zimri has plotted, and he has even struck down the king," all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that very day in the camp.

L.16: And the people who were encamped heard, saying, "Zimri has conspired, and he has also struck down the king." And all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel on that day in the camp.

R.16: The soldiers in the camp heard people say, "Zimri has made plans against the king, and he has killed him!" So that same day, there in the camp, all the Israelites made Omri, the army commander, king over Israel.

decisions.choice: all Israel: Israel's fighting men gathered at the camp
decisions.reason: The ones who make Omri king are the army in the field. In verses 21-22 the people as a whole are divided over him.

decisions.choice: Omri, commander of the army: the general set against the chariot officer
decisions.reason: The army chose its own commander over Zimri, who commanded only half the chariots (verse 9). Omri's family background is not given.

decisions.choice: saying: the report as it went round the camp
decisions.reason: The word introduces the news in the words people used.

decisions.choice: all the Israelites (there in the camp)
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "all Israel" here means those in the camp (m1).

records.source: וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה עָמְרִ֛י וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ מִֽגִּבְּת֑וֹן וַיָּצֻ֖רוּ עַל־תִּרְצָֽה׃
records.gloss: And went up Omri and all Israel with him from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.
pieces: Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and laid siege to Tirzah.

L.17: And Omri went up, and all Israel with him, from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.

R.17: Then Omri and all the Israelite troops with him left Gibbethon. They went up to Tirzah and surrounded it.

decisions.choice: went up from Gibbethon: from the lowland to the hill country
decisions.reason: Gibbethon lay in the low hills toward the coast, Tirzah in the hill country of Ephraim and Manasseh, so the army "went up".

decisions.choice: all the Israelite troops
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Readable says "all Israel" means the army.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י כִּרְא֤וֹת זִמְרִי֙ כִּֽי־נִלְכְּדָ֣ה הָעִ֔יר וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־אַרְמ֣וֹן בֵּית־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׂרֹ֨ף עָלָ֧יו אֶת־בֵּֽית־מֶ֛לֶךְ בָּאֵ֖שׁ וַיָּמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And it was, when saw Zimri that was captured the city, and he went into [the] citadel of [the] house of the king, and burned over himself [the] house of [the] king with fire, and died,
pieces: When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he went into the citadel of the royal palace and set the palace on fire over himself, and he died,

L.18: And it happened, when Zimri saw that the city was captured, he went into the citadel of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire, and he died,

R.18: When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the strongest part of the palace. He set the palace on fire around himself and died in the flames.

decisions.choice: the citadel of the king's house: the fortified keep of the palace
decisions.reason: The word names the strongest, most defended building or tower of a palace, where a king could make a last stand.

decisions.choice: burned the house over himself: chose death rather than capture
decisions.reason: Zimri set the palace alight with himself inside. His death left Tirzah without a palace, which may be part of why Omri later built a new capital (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the strongest part of the palace
decisions.reason: Readable explains "citadel".

records.source: עַל־חַטֹּאתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם וּבְחַטָּאתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לְהַחֲטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: because of his sins which he sinned, to do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, to walk in [the] way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he did, to make sin Israel.
pieces: because of the sins he had committed, doing what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he committed, by which he led Israel to sin.

L.19: because of his sins which he sinned, doing the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he did, to make Israel sin.

R.19: He died because of his sins. He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He lived the way Jeroboam had lived and committed the sin by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: doing the evil in the eyes of Yahweh: doing what Yahweh judges evil
decisions.reason: "In the eyes of" means in someone's judgment. This is the standard verdict on a king in Kings (11:6; 15:26, 34), as in Judges (2:11).

decisions.choice: his sins: the standard verdict, even for a reign of seven days
decisions.reason: Zimri had little time to do anything as king, but the writer counts him with the kings who followed Jeroboam's way, and sees his death as judgment on his sin, the murder of his king included.

decisions.choice: his sin which he did: Jeroboam's sin
decisions.reason: "His" here refers to Jeroboam, the sin of the calves by which Jeroboam led Israel to sin (verse 2).

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings, as in Judges.

decisions.choice: the sin by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: Readable names Jeroboam to make "his" clear (m3).

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י זִמְרִ֔י וְקִשְׁר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר הֲלֹֽא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Zimri and his conspiracy which he conspired, [are] they not written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Zimri, and the conspiracy he carried out, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.20: And the rest of the matters of Zimri, and his conspiracy that he conspired, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.20: Everything else Zimri did, and how he plotted against the king, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: his conspiracy which he conspired: the plot by which he took the throne
decisions.reason: The noun and verb from the same root stress that Zimri is remembered for his treason. The phrase is used again of Shallum (2 Kings 15:15).

decisions.choice: the source formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: אָ֧ז יֵחָלֵ֛ק הָעָ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַחֵ֑צִי חֲצִ֨י הָעָ֜ם הָ֠יָה אַחֲרֵ֨י תִבְנִ֤י בֶן־גִּינַת֙ לְהַמְלִיכ֔וֹ וְהַחֲצִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֥י עָמְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: Then was divided the people Israel into half; half of the people was after Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and the half after Omri.
pieces: Then the people of Israel were split in two. Half the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and the other half followed Omri.

L.21: Then the people Israel were divided into halves: half of the people were after Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, and half [were] after Omri.

R.21: Then the people of Israel were divided into two groups. Half of them followed Tibni son of Ginath and wanted to make him king. The other half followed Omri.

decisions.choice: were after: followed and supported
decisions.reason: To be "after" someone is to follow him as a leader (2 Samuel 2:10; 15:13).

decisions.choice: Tibni son of Ginath: a rival claimant otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: Nothing more is known of Tibni. The struggle seems to have lasted about four years, from Asa's twenty-seventh year (verse 15) to his thirty-first (verse 23).

records.heading: Omri king of Israel

records.source: וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַחֲרֵ֣י עָמְרִ֔י אֶת־הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַחֲרֵ֖י תִּבְנִ֣י בֶן־גִּינַ֑ת וַיָּ֣מָת תִּבְנִ֔י וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עָמְרִֽי׃פ
records.gloss: And prevailed the people who [were] after Omri over the people who [were] after Tibni son of Ginath; and died Tibni, and reigned Omri.
pieces: But the people who followed Omri were stronger than the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.

L.22: And the people who [were] after Omri prevailed over the people who [were] after Tibni son of Ginath, and Tibni died, and Omri reigned.

R.22: But Omri's followers were stronger than Tibni's followers. Tibni died, and Omri became king.

decisions.choice: Tibni died, and Omri reigned: the two facts set side by side
decisions.reason: The text does not say how Tibni died, whether in battle, by execution or otherwise. It simply joins his death to Omri's taking the throne.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וְאַחַ֜ת שָׁנָ֗ה לְאָסָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה מָלַ֤ךְ עָמְרִי֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה בְּתִרְצָ֖ה מָלַ֥ךְ שֵׁשׁ־שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: In year thirty and one year of Asa king of Judah reigned Omri over Israel twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.
pieces: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

L.23: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri reigned over Israel twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.

R.23: Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-first year that Asa was king of Judah. He ruled for twelve years, and for six of those years he ruled in Tirzah.

decisions.choice: the thirty-first year ... twelve years: his sole rule and his whole reign
decisions.reason: Omri was made king in Asa's twenty-seventh year (verses 15-16) and Ahab followed him in Asa's thirty-eighth (verse 29). The twelve years seem to be counted from his first claim, with the thirty-first year marking when Tibni died and Omri ruled alone.

decisions.choice: in Tirzah six years: before the move to Samaria
decisions.reason: The rest of his reign was in Samaria, the city he built (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the accession formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

records.source: וַיִּ֜קֶן אֶת־הָהָ֥ר שֹׁמְר֛וֹן מֵ֥אֶת שֶׁ֖מֶר בְּכִכְּרַ֣יִם כָּ֑סֶף וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־הָהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־שֵׁ֤ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה עַ֣ל שֶׁם־שֶׁ֔מֶר אֲדֹנֵ֖י הָהָ֥ר שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he bought the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents [of] silver; and he built [on] the hill, and called [the] name of the city which he built after [the] name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria.
pieces: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for {{units:about 150 pounds|two talents}} of silver. He built a city on the hill and named it Samaria, after Shemer, the owner of the hill.

L.24: And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and he built [on] the hill, and he called the name of the city that he built after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill: Samaria.

R.24: Omri bought the hill of Samaria from a man named Shemer. He paid {{units:about 150 pounds|two talents}} of silver for it. He built a city on the hill and named it Samaria, after Shemer, who had owned the hill.

decisions.choice: Samaria: a name drawn from Shemer
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name *Shomron* sounds like Shemer, the hill's owner. It may also suggest a "watch" place, since the hill stands alone and overlooks the land around it.

decisions.choice: he bought and built: a new royal city on land the king owned
decisions.reason: Like David with Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:6-9), Omri made a capital that belonged to the crown and to no tribe. Samaria stayed the capital of Israel until it fell to Assyria (2 Kings 17:5-6), and the whole kingdom came to be called by its name.

decisions.choice: two talents of silver: a large sum
decisions.reason: A talent was about 75 pounds, so the price was about 150 pounds of silver. The silver was weighed, not coined.

decisions.choice: owner: a plural form used for one owner
decisions.reason: The word for "owner" (literally "lords") is plural in form, as it often is for a master or owner; Shemer alone is meant.

decisions.choice: about 150 pounds / two talents
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the original unit as the alternative; Literal keeps the unit.

decisions.choice: built [on] the hill
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "built the hill"; the sense is that he built a city on it, as the next words say.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עָמְרִ֛י הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּ֕רַע מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And did Omri the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and did evil more than all who [were] before him.
pieces: Omri did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He did more evil than all who were before him.

L.25: And Omri did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he did more evil than all who [were] before him.

R.25: Omri did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did even more evil than all the kings before him.

decisions.choice: more evil than all before him: the decline of the northern kings
decisions.reason: Each verdict now goes further: Omri outdoes those before him, and his son Ahab will outdo him (verses 30, 33). The writer gives Omri only a few verses, though he was a strong king whose house ruled Israel for three generations.

decisions.choice: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.choice: all the kings before him
decisions.reason: Readable names those he is compared with, the kings of Israel before him (verse 33).

records.source: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּכָל־דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט וּבְחַטָּאת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְהַכְעִ֗יס אֶת־יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּהַבְלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And he walked in all [the] way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin which he made sin Israel, to provoke Yahweh God of Israel with their vanities.
pieces: He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin, by which he led Israel to sin, provoking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.

L.26: And he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sin which he made Israel sin, to provoke {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel to anger with their worthless idols.

R.26: He lived in every way as Jeroboam son of Nebat had lived. He committed the sin by which Jeroboam led Israel into sin. So they made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, angry with their useless idols.

decisions.choice: his sin which he made Israel sin: Jeroboam's sin
decisions.reason: As in verse 19, "his" is Jeroboam; the sin is the worship at the calf shrines.

decisions.choice: their vanities: their worthless idols
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the formulas of the sin of Jeroboam and of provoking to anger
decisions.reason: As in verses 2 and 13.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י עָמְרִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וּגְבוּרָת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹֽא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Omri which he did and his might which he did, [are] they not written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Omri, what he did and the might he showed, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.27: And the rest of the matters of Omri that he did, and his might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.27: Everything else Omri did, and his great deeds, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: his might: deeds of power
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Omri was a strong king, though the writer tells little about it beyond the founding of Samaria.

decisions.choice: the source formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 5. Literal says "showed" for the second "did", which English does not use with "might".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב עָמְרִי֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אַחְאָ֥ב בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Omri with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and reigned Ahab his son in his place.
pieces: Omri rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king in his place.

L.28: And Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his place.

R.28: Omri died and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: As in verse 6. Omri is the first king buried in Samaria, the city he founded.

decisions.choice: the death formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

records.source: וְאַחְאָ֣ב בֶּן־עָמְרִ֗י מָלַךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַ֠יִּמְלֹךְ אַחְאָ֨ב בֶּן־עָמְרִ֤י עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in year thirty and eight year of Asa king of Judah; and reigned Ahab son of Omri over Israel in Samaria twenty and two year[s].
pieces: Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

L.29: And Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

R.29: Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year that Asa was king of Judah. Ahab ruled over Israel from Samaria for twenty-two years.

decisions.choice: Ahab son of Omri, named twice: a solemn opening
decisions.reason: The formula is fuller than usual, naming Ahab and his father twice. It marks the start of the long account of Ahab's reign and of Elijah, which runs to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: the accession formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 8. Balanced keeps both halves as the Hebrew has them.

records.heading: Ahab king of Israel

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ אַחְאָ֧ב בֶּן־עָמְרִ֛י הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And did Ahab son of Omri the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh more than all who [were] before him.
pieces: Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, more than all who were before him.

L.30: And Ahab son of Omri did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} more than all who [were] before him.

R.30: Ahab son of Omri did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. He did more evil than all the kings before him.

decisions.choice: more than all before him: Ahab outdoes even Omri
decisions.reason: The same words were said of Omri (verse 25). Ahab goes further still, as verses 31-33 show.

decisions.choice: the verdict formula
decisions.reason: As in verse 19. Readable names "the kings", as in verse 25.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ הֲנָקֵ֣ל לֶכְתּ֔וֹ בְּחַטֹּ֖אות יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וַיִּקַּ֨ח אִשָּׁ֜ה אֶת־אִיזֶ֗בֶל בַּת־אֶתְבַּ֨עַל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ צִידֹנִ֔ים וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֣ד אֶת־הַבַּ֔עַל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, was it a light thing, his walking in [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat? And he took [as] wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of [the] Sidonians, and he went and served the Baal and bowed down to him.
pieces: As though walking in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat were a small thing for him, he married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

L.31: And it was, as if it were a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, that he took a wife, Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and went and served the Baal and bowed down to him.

R.31: It was not enough for him to commit the same sins as Jeroboam son of Nebat. He also married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Then he began to serve the god Baal and bowed down to worship him.

decisions.choice: was it a light thing ...?: as if Jeroboam's sins were too little
decisions.reason: The Hebrew asks, "Was it a trifling thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam?" The question means that Ahab treated those sins as not enough and went further.

decisions.choice: Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians: a Phoenician princess
decisions.reason: "Sidonians" is the name for the Phoenicians of the coast, whose chief cities were Sidon and Tyre. Ethbaal's name means "with Baal". The marriage was an alliance, but it brought the worship of Baal into Israel's palace (18:19; 21:25).

decisions.choice: the Baal: the Canaanite storm god
decisions.reason: Baal was worshiped as the god who sends rain and makes the land fruitful (Judges 6:25). The story of Elijah and the drought that follows (17:1; 18:21-39) is a contest over who truly gives rain.

decisions.choice: he went and served: he turned to the worship of Baal
decisions.reason: "Went and" marks the start of a new course: Ahab himself became a worshiper of Baal.

decisions.choice: as if it were a light thing (Literal); as though ... were a small thing (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced turn the question into a clause that keeps its point; Readable says it plainly: "It was not enough".

decisions.choice: the god Baal
decisions.reason: Readable says who Baal was, as in Judges 6:25.

records.source: וַיָּ֥קֶם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַבָּ֑עַל בֵּ֣ית הַבַּ֔עַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he set up an altar to the Baal [in the] house of the Baal which he built in Samaria.
pieces: He set up an altar to Baal in the temple of Baal that he had built in Samaria.

L.32: And he set up an altar for the Baal [in] the house of the Baal that he built in Samaria.

R.32: He built a temple for Baal in Samaria and set up an altar for Baal in it.

decisions.choice: the house of Baal: a temple to Baal
decisions.reason: "House" of a god means a temple. Ahab built one in his own capital, a rival to Yahweh's temple. Jehu later tore it down (2 Kings 10:21-27).

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for the house of a god; Literal keeps "house".

decisions.choice: He built a temple ... and set up an altar
decisions.reason: Readable tells the building of the temple first, then the altar in it.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אַחְאָ֖ב אֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרָ֑ה וַיּ֨וֹסֶף אַחְאָ֜ב לַעֲשׂ֗וֹת לְהַכְעִיס֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִכֹּ֨ל מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And made Ahab the Asherah, and added Ahab to do, to provoke Yahweh God of Israel, more than all [the] kings of Israel who were before him.
pieces: Ahab also made the Asherah pole. He did more than all the kings of Israel before him to provoke {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, to anger.

L.33: And Ahab made the Asherah pole, and Ahab did more to provoke {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel who were before him.

R.33: Ahab also set up a pole used to worship Asherah. He did more to make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, angry than all the kings of Israel before him.

decisions.choice: the Asherah: a wooden pole for the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and her symbol, a wooden pole or tree, stood by an altar (Judges 6:25). Israel had been told to cut such poles down (Exodus 34:13; Deuteronomy 7:5). The article may point to a pole set up with Baal's altar in Samaria.

decisions.choice: added to do, to provoke: did still more to provoke
decisions.reason: "Added to do" means he went on doing more. The chapter's verdicts build to this point: Ahab is the worst king of Israel so far.

decisions.choice: Asherah pole (Literal, Balanced); a pole used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for Asherah poles in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: provoke to anger / make angry
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: בְּיָמָ֞יו בָּנָ֥ה חִיאֵ֛ל בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלִ֖י אֶת־יְרִיחֹ֑ה בַּאֲבִירָ֨ם בְּכֹר֜וֹ יִסְּדָ֗הּ וּבִשְׂג֤וּב צְעִירוֹ֙ הִצִּ֣יב דְּלָתֶ֔יהָ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בִּן־נֽוּן׃ס
records.gloss: In his days built Hiel the Bethelite Jericho; with Abiram his firstborn he founded it, and with Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of Joshua son of Nun.
pieces: In Ahab's days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. At the price of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the price of Segub his youngest he set its gates in place, as the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Joshua son of Nun.

L.34: In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. With Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and with Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.

R.34: While Ahab was king, Hiel from Bethel built the city of Jericho again. His oldest son, Abiram, died when he laid its foundation. His youngest son, Segub, died when he put up its gates. This happened just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Joshua son of Nun.

decisions.choice: Joshua's curse on Jericho comes true
decisions.reason: After Jericho fell, Joshua put the people under oath that whoever rebuilt the city would lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son (Joshua 6:26). This verse repeats the words of that oath almost exactly, with three differences: the verbs are now past, telling what happened; the two sons are named, Abiram and Segub; and the curse formula itself ("cursed before Yahweh be the man") is not repeated. Building the foundation and the gates are the first and last stages of a walled city.

decisions.choice: with Abiram ... with Segub: at the cost of his sons
alternatives: Hiel sacrificed his sons in the building
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 6:26, "with" gives the price paid: the eldest son died when the work began and the youngest when it was finished. The text does not say how they died. Some have thought Hiel offered them as foundation sacrifices; the verse itself presents their deaths as the curse taking effect.

decisions.choice: Hiel the Bethelite: a man from Bethel
decisions.reason: Bethel was the site of Jeroboam's calf shrine (12:29), a few miles from Jericho. Jericho had been lived in before (Judges 3:13; 2 Samuel 10:5), but Hiel rebuilt it as a walled city.

decisions.choice: in his days: in Ahab's reign
decisions.reason: The note sets Hiel's work under Ahab: in a reign that defied Yahweh, his word through Joshua still came true.

decisions.choice: At the price of ... set its gates in place (Balanced); died when he laid ... put up its gates (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable reuse the wording of Joshua 6:26 at each level, so the fulfillment can be heard.

decisions.choice: In Ahab's days (Balanced); While Ahab was king (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Ahab for "his" (m4).
